scenes.title: Marley Was Dead
scenes.summary: The narrator insists Marley is unquestionably dead, witnessed and signed for, establishing that any wonder to follow must be supernatural.

scenes.title: Scrooge the Miser
scenes.summary: Scrooge is introduced as Marley's surviving partner: a cold, miserly, solitary man whom no one approaches and who prefers to be left alone.

muse_override.reason: Frosty solitary miser description creates bleak, mysterious gloom with no warmth.

scenes.title: Christmas Eve Counting-House
scenes.summary: On a foggy, freezing Christmas Eve, Scrooge watches his shivering clerk from his counting-house, hoarding coal and warmth.

scenes.title: Nephew's Merry Christmas
scenes.summary: Scrooge's cheerful nephew wishes him merry Christmas; Scrooge calls it humbug and they debate wealth, merriment, and the meaning of Christmas.

muse_override.reason: Cheerful nephew's warmth clashes playfully with Scrooge's gruff humbug retorts.

scenes.title: Dinner Refused
scenes.summary: The clerk applauds and is threatened, the nephew's dinner invitation is repeatedly refused with 'Good afternoon,' and he leaves kindly greeting the clerk.

muse_override.reason: Cold verbal sparring and repeated dismissal create combative tension tinged with lonely sadness against cheerful persistence.

scenes.title: No Gift for the Poor
scenes.summary: Two charity collectors ask for help for the poor; Scrooge cites prisons, workhouses and the Poor Law, refuses to give, and dismisses them.

muse_override.reason: Cold refusal of charity evokes sorrowful bleakness with moral confrontation.

scenes.title: Fog and Festivity
scenes.summary: Fog and Christmas bustle fill London with shops, fires and merrymaking while Scrooge drives away a carol singer with a ruler.

scenes.title: Shutting Up
scenes.summary: Scrooge grudgingly grants Christmas Day off, threatens to dock pay, then leaves the clerk to slide and run home to play.

muse_override.reason: Grumbling miserliness yields to the clerk's exuberant Christmas Eve joy.

scenes.title: The Knocker's Face
scenes.summary: Scrooge dines alone and returns to his gloomy chambers, where the door knocker impossibly transforms into Marley's face, then back again.

scenes.title: Up the Dark Stairs
scenes.summary: Shaken but defiant, Scrooge bolts inside, climbs the dark staircase imagining a hearse, and searches every room to reassure himself.

scenes.title: Face in the Tiles
scenes.summary: Huddled over a low fire, Scrooge sees Marley's face haunting the Dutch tiles, dismisses it as humbug, then watches a disused bell begin to swing and ring with all the bells in the house.

muse_override.reason: Marley's haunting face and self-swinging bells build uncanny mystery with rising suspense.

scenes.title: Bells and Chains
scenes.summary: As the bells fall silent, a chain clanks up from the cellar toward his door; Scrooge insists it is humbug until the sound passes through the heavy door and the flame leaps at Marley's Ghost.

scenes.title: Marley's Ghost Appears
scenes.summary: Marley's Ghost enters through the locked door, transparent and bound in cash-boxes and ledgers, chilling Scrooge who fights his senses.

scenes.title: Who Are You
scenes.summary: Scrooge demands who he wants; the shade declares he was Jacob Marley and, despite doubts, sits by the fireplace to talk.

scenes.title: Humbug and Undigested Beef
scenes.summary: Scrooge dismisses the ghost as indigestion, gravy rather than grave, trying to joke away terror as the spectre watches unmoved.

muse_override.reason: Scrooge's terrified denial of the chilling ghost blends dread and supernatural mystery with awe.

scenes.title: The Chain Forged in Life
scenes.summary: The ghost shrieks, drops its jaw, and explains spirits must wander after death; Scrooge learns he forges a ponderous chain like Marley's.

muse_override.reason: Marley's rattling chain and fallen jaw mix dread mystery with mournful regret for a life misspent.

scenes.title: Mankind Was My Business
scenes.summary: Marley laments restless wandering, crying that mankind, charity and mercy were his true business, not trade, flinging down his chain.

scenes.title: Three Spirits Foretold
scenes.summary: Marley warns Scrooge he may yet escape his fate, prophesying visits from three spirits on the next three nights at one and twelve.

muse_override.reason: Marley's mournful warning of three spirits creates dread-filled suspense and supernatural mystery.

scenes.title: Phantoms in the Air
scenes.summary: Marley floats out the window into a night of wailing chained phantoms; Scrooge shuts the window, cannot say humbug, and falls asleep.

muse_override.reason: Wailing chained phantoms lamenting lost power evoke sorrowful mystery and dread.

scenes.title: The Impossible Twelve
scenes.summary: Scrooge wakes in darkness and hears a church bell run up to twelve, fears he has slept through a day, and is relieved to find it still night outside.

muse_override.reason: Scrooge's impossible midnight bell creates uncanny mystery and stunned astonishment at broken time.

scenes.title: Awake Until One
scenes.summary: Back in bed, Scrooge puzzles over whether Marley's Ghost was a dream and resolves to lie awake until the promised visitation at one.

scenes.title: The Hour Strikes One
scenes.summary: Scrooge counts the quarters to the hour, hears melancholy One strike, sees light flash, and finds his bed curtains drawn by an unearthly visitor standing at his elbow.

scenes.title: Ghost of Christmas Past
scenes.summary: The strange child-like Spirit with a jet of light from its head reveals itself as the Ghost of Christmas Past, warns against extinguishing its light, and commands Scrooge to rise and walk with him for his reclamation.

scenes.title: Through the Wall
scenes.summary: Touched on the heart by the Spirit, Scrooge passes through the wall to a clear winter day on his boyhood country road, overwhelmed by long-forgotten smells and feelings.

scenes.title: Every Gate and Tree
scenes.summary: Hiding his tears, Scrooge joyfully remembers the way and recognizes every gate, post, and tree as they walk toward the market-town amid merry schoolboys.

scenes.title: The Solitary Child
scenes.summary: At the lonely broken-down school, Scrooge weeps to see his forgotten solitary self reading by a feeble fire, rejoices in imaginary friends like Ali Baba and Robinson Crusoe, and regrets not giving to the carol singer.

scenes.title: Fan Comes to Bring Him Home
scenes.summary: Little Fan bursts in to bring her brother home for Christmas forever, a joyful rescue shadowed when the Ghost reveals she later died leaving one child, Scrooge's nephew.

scenes.title: Fezziwig's Warehouse
scenes.summary: In a bustling Christmas city, Scrooge recognizes his apprenticeship at Fezziwig's warehouse as old Fezziwig shouts for work to stop and the apprentices race to shutter and clear the room for a party.

scenes.title: The Christmas Ball
scenes.summary: The warehouse becomes a bright ballroom full of dancing, feasting, and Sir Roger de Coverley, until Scrooge defends Fezziwig's small expense as great happiness and wishes he could speak to his own clerk.

scenes.title: The Golden Idol
scenes.summary: Shown older and grasping, Scrooge watches his beloved Belle in mourning release him because gain has displaced love, and they part as she wishes him happiness in the life he chose.

scenes.title: A Tumultuous Family Christmas
scenes.summary: Scrooge begs the Ghost to show him no more, but is pinioned and forced to watch. They see Belle grown into a comely matron with her daughter in a small, comfortable room overrun with boisterous children, followed by the joyful homecoming of the father laden with Christmas toys and presents.

scenes.title: Quite Alone in the World
scenes.summary: Watching Belle's family gathered tenderly at the fireside, Scrooge imagines the daughter who might have called him father. He hears her husband tell how he saw Scrooge sitting alone at his office while his partner lay dying, quite alone in the world. Broken, Scrooge begs for removal and turns to wrestle the Ghost.

scenes.title: Crushing the Light
scenes.summary: Crying to be taken back and haunted no longer, Scrooge seizes the Ghost's extinguisher-cap and presses it down to crush its burning light. The light streams from under it in an unbroken flood as Scrooge, exhausted and drowsy, finds himself in his own bedroom and sinks into heavy sleep.

scenes.title: Waiting Past One in Ruddy Light
scenes.summary: Scrooge wakes ready to confront the second spirit, but when one o'clock strikes no shape appears and he trembles in a blaze of ruddy light, until he traces its source to the adjoining room.

scenes.title: Discovery of the Feast and Jolly Giant
scenes.summary: Called by name, Scrooge enters to find his room transformed into a green grove heaped with a great feast, presided over by a jolly giant holding a glowing torch aloft.

muse_override.reason: Lavish feast and jolly giant radiate joyful wonder with slight mystery.

scenes.title: I Am Christmas Present
scenes.summary: The jolly Spirit introduces himself as the Ghost of Christmas Present, shows his green robe and rusted scabbard, claims eighteen hundred brothers, and Scrooge submits to be taught and touches his robe.

muse_override.reason: Jolly, genial Ghost inspires warm joy with wondrous awe at its grandeur.

scenes.title: Christmas Morning in the City
scenes.summary: Transported to Christmas morning streets, Scrooge watches snow-clearing, jovial crowds, radiant poulterers, fruiterers, and bustling grocers full of hurried, eager customers.

scenes.title: Blessing of Dinners and Rebuke
scenes.summary: Beside bakers' shops the Spirit blesses poor dinners and restores quarrels with his torch, then rebukes Scrooge for blaming Spirits for Sabbatarian closing of dining places.

muse_override.reason: Warm torch blessing over poor dinners then solemn rebuke evokes calm joy and awe, not battle.

scenes.title: Arrival at the Cratchits
scenes.summary: The Spirit blesses the Cratchit home where Mrs. Cratchit prepares, Martha returns late from work, Bob arrives with Tiny Tim on his shoulder, and the family gathers excitedly for the goose.

scenes.title: Goose and Glorious Pudding
scenes.summary: The Cratchits celebrate their Christmas goose with universal admiration, then anxiously await the pudding, which Mrs. Cratchit brings in blazing triumphantly. After dinner they gather round the hearth for Bob's toast, echoed by Tiny Tim's blessing as Bob holds his little hand.

scenes.title: Vacant Seat and Prophecy
scenes.summary: Scrooge asks if Tiny Tim will live and the Spirit shows him a vacant seat and ownerless crutch, foretelling the child's death. When Scrooge pleads, the Ghost turns his own words about surplus population against him and rebukes him for judging who shall live.

scenes.title: The Founder of the Feast Toast
scenes.summary: Bob proposes a toast to Scrooge as Founder of the Feast, Mrs. Cratchit protests bitterly but drinks for Bob's sake, and the mention of Scrooge casts a shadow over the party.

scenes.title: Merriment After the Shadow
scenes.summary: With Scrooge dismissed, the Cratchits grow merrier over Peter's prospects, Martha's work, and Tiny Tim's song, leaving Scrooge watching them, especially Tiny Tim, with new tenderness.

scenes.title: Christmas Far and Wide
scenes.summary: Roving through snowy night streets, a bleak miner's moor hut, a solitary lighthouse, and a ship at sea, Scrooge sees everywhere fires, song, and kinder Christmas thoughts shared.

scenes.title: Nephew Fred's Laughing Party
scenes.summary: In Fred's bright gleaming room, Scrooge watches contagious laughter, teasing about Christmas as humbug, defense of pitying Scrooge, and vows to give him the same chance yearly.

scenes.title: Games and Toast to Uncle Scrooge
scenes.summary: Music recalls Scrooge's childhood, then blind-man's buff, forfeits, and the Yes and No game reveal Uncle Scrooge the animal, ending in a sincere toast that softens Scrooge to gay lightness.

scenes.title: The Spirit Grows Old
scenes.summary: After visiting many homes, hospitals, and prisons with blessing, Scrooge notices the night condensed and the Spirit visibly older, whose life ends tonight at midnight.

muse_override.reason: Warm blessings turn bittersweet as the aging Spirit nears midnight, mixing joy with suspenseful loss.

scenes.title: The Children Beneath the Robe
scenes.summary: Scrooge notices something strange protruding from the Spirit's robe, and the Spirit reveals two wretched, hideous children, a boy and girl, clinging to its garment and bids Scrooge look upon them.

scenes.title: Doom and the Approaching Phantom
scenes.summary: The Spirit names the children Ignorance and Want, warns of Doom written on the boy unless erased, turns Scrooge's own words about prisons and workhouses upon him, then vanishes at twelve as a hooded Phantom approaches.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: Meeting the Silent Phantom
scenes.summary: The silent, black-shrouded Phantom approaches. Scrooge trembles with solemn dread, begs it to speak and to lead on, and follows in the shadow of its dress.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: Gossip on 'Change
scenes.summary: On 'Change among the merchants, Scrooge overhears a knot of businessmen joking coldly about a dead man no one will mourn or bury, and looks to the Spirit for explanation.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: A Trivial Meeting and a Missing Self
scenes.summary: The Phantom shows another trivial exchange about 'old Scratch' getting his own. Scrooge searches in vain for his future self on his accustomed corner and feels chilled by the Spirit's keen gaze.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: Old Joe's Den
scenes.summary: They enter a foul, criminal slum to a rag-and-bone shop where old Joe smokes by his stove. Three plunderers meet laughing and are led into the parlour behind the rags.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: Bargaining Over Spoil
scenes.summary: The women defend robbing the dead man who lived alone and unloved. The undertaker's man and Mrs. Dilber sell small seals, buttons, sheets, spoons and boots to Joe for chalked sums.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

muse_override.reason: Sordid haggling over a dead man's goods blends bleak cynicism with tense illicit secrecy.

scenes.title: The Stolen Shroud
scenes.summary: The first woman triumphantly sells bed-curtains, blankets and even the shirt meant for burial, stripped from the corpse. Scrooge watches in horror as they laugh that his loneliness profited them, and realizes the case might be his own.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

muse_override.reason: Scrooge watches thieves strip his corpse with cold laughter and realizes in horror it could be his own fate.

scenes.title: The Bare Bed
scenes.summary: The scene shifts to a dark, bare bedroom where the plundered corpse lies unwatched, unwept and uncared for. Scrooge dares not lift the veil, begs to leave, and pleads to be shown some emotion caused by the death.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: Anxious Waiting for News
scenes.summary: The Phantom reveals a sunlit room where a debtor wife anxiously awaits her husband. He returns careworn yet with repressed delight and tells her their creditor is past relenting because he is dead, and she is inwardly thankful to hear it.
characters: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: Lighter Hearts in a Happier House
scenes.summary: The husband explains the creditor was dying when delay was refused, and hopes for a more merciful successor. Their hearts are lighter and the house is happier for the man's death, giving Scrooge only pleasure.
characters: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

muse_override.reason: Relief from debt after the creditor's death makes the house lighter and happier.

scenes.title: Mourning Tiny Tim
scenes.summary: At Bob Cratchit's quiet house the family sews in grief. Peter reads of Christ and the child. Bob returns late from the green churchyard, breaks down for his little child, and sits reconciled beside the Christmas-hung upstairs room.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: We Shall Not Forget Poor Tiny Tim
scenes.summary: Around the fire Bob tells of Scrooge's nephew's extraordinary kindness and offer of help. They vow never to forget patient, mild Tiny Tim nor quarrel in his memory, and Scrooge demands to know who lay dead.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: The Neglected Grave
scenes.summary: Hurried past business resorts to his own office, now occupied by another, Scrooge is led to a choked churchyard. Before the pointed grave he begs to know if these are shadows of what Will be or only what May be.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

muse_override.reason: Scrooge's dreadful discovery of his own neglected grave is dominated by suspense and sorrow with cold mystery.

scenes.title: I Will Not Be That Man
scenes.summary: Reading EBENEZER SCROOGE on the stone, he clutches the robe in agony, vows to honour Christmas and live in Past, Present and Future, and to sponge away the writing. The Phantom shrinks into a bedpost.
characters: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

scenes.title: Awake and Redeemed
scenes.summary: Scrooge wakes in his own bed on Christmas morning, weeping and laughing with relief that the shadows can be dispelled. He frisks about the rooms, vowing to live in Past, Present and Future, and rejoices at the bells, sunlight and clear air.

scenes.title: The Prize Turkey
scenes.summary: From his window Scrooge learns it is Christmas Day and gleefully sends a boy to buy the prize turkey. He has it delivered to Bob Cratchit's, loving his door-knocker and chuckling till he cries with playful generosity.

scenes.title: Christmas Streets and Amends
scenes.summary: Shaved and dressed in his best, Scrooge walks the streets smiling at everyone. He stops the portly charity gentleman to beg pardon and whisper a large donation, then spends the day in church and happy wandering.

scenes.title: Dinner at Fred's
scenes.summary: Nervous but determined, Scrooge knocks at his nephew Fred's house and begs to come to dinner. He is welcomed heartily and joins a wonderful party with Fred, his niece, Topper and all the guests in unanimous happiness.

scenes.title: The Late Clerk
scenes.summary: Early at the office next morning, Scrooge lies in wait to catch Bob Cratchit eighteen minutes late. Feigning his old growl, he sternly calls Bob in, frightening him into thinking he will be scolded or seized.

scenes.title: A Merrier Christmas and Ever After
scenes.summary: Scrooge reveals the trick with a dig in the waistcoat and raises Bob's salary, promising to help his family over smoking bishop. Transformed into a good master and second father to Tiny Tim, he learns to keep Christmas well ever after.

rejected.reason: After 21-22 remains stern confrontation ('sternly, keep Christmas in your own way'), dominant feeling stays combate/indignation, no sustained shift to alegria despite vector claim.

Paragraph 619 is still transition/mystery (rejoining Phantom, iron gate) rather than the tristeza of the churchyard in 620, and the right mood is a mixed tristeza+suspenso blend without a strong single dominant replacing misterio, so no strong sustained dominant change at 619.
